milestones.name: On the Mac, one cooked mesh is culled and drawn a meshlet at a time by the GPU's object and mesh stages, and the picture matches the path it replaces
milestones.quality_bar: A meshlet path as a shipped GPU-driven renderer has one, such as Alan Wake 2's mesh-shader geometry: the player cannot tell it from drawing everything. Held to that literally: the same bytes with the cull on as with it off.

items.statement: A launch that names `mesh-stages` on this Mac gets a device with the object and mesh stages enabled and their limits, and the registry reports them. A launch that names nothing gets the device it gets today. An unknown name, and `mesh-stages` on an adapter that does not offer them, are each refused by name before a device is made.
items.ask: Is there one function in the registry that turns a launch's list into the device request, shared with `ray-query`, and does every host that asks go through it?

items.statement: On a cooked mesh that has meshlets facing away, meshlets outside the view and meshlets cut by each frustum plane, the mesh-stage path's submitted bytes with its cull on equal its bytes with the cull off, at every frame of a scripted camera path that turns, passes through the mesh and crosses a cut.
items.ask: Does the proof assert that the cull rejected meshlets for each reason (the cone, each plane) on that path, with a count that is not zero, so the equality is not vacuous? Is the cull's rule one function text compiled into both the compute pass and the object stage?

items.statement: The difference between the mesh-stage path with its cull off and the indirect path, on the same fixed views, is measured and on record with its cause: the largest difference in each stored channel of colour, depth, motion and reactive coverage, how many pixels differ, and where they lie. A pixel that differs away from a triangle's edge or a depth tie is a defect that is fixed, not a figure that is recorded.
items.ask: Does the record show that every differing pixel lies on a triangle's edge or a depth tie, with the cause found and not assumed? Is the bound M1.4 holds the measured one and not a wider one?

items.statement: A mesh-stage frame matches the indirect path's within M1.3's record: lit, shadowed and textured, with motion and reactive coverage, with history valid and in the first frame after a cut.

The frame reports the cooked path it resolved to. `Auto` is the path chosen today. An explicit `MeshStages` on a device without the stages is refused by name when the scene is prepared. On the mesh-stage path the forward pass records one mesh draw for each placement, and no cull pass and no indexed indirect draw for it.
items.ask: Is the report the resolved path and not an echo of the request, so that the indirect path cannot pass as the mesh stages?

items.statement: The pipelines of the stages and of the indirect fallback are created before the scene is ready, through the device's creation authority, and the ledger counts them. A stages pipeline that fails to build resolves its mesh to the indirect path before the scene is ready, and the report says so. None is created while the scene runs.

A device without the stages uploads no meshlet storage, and its resident bytes are those of main. With the stages, a mesh's meshlet storage is copied under the upload budget with the mesh and counted in its residency.
No exact baseline moves: with no request, and on the direct and indirect paths, every registered image on the Mac's two recipes and in Chrome is the one on main.

milestones.name: The valley's terrain and cooked meshes draw through the object and mesh stages in the main view and the Sun's shadow maps, through edits and device loss, with the cost of both paths on record
milestones.quality_bar: The valley as it is drawn today, with no hole, flicker or popping meshlet anywhere on the route, and a cost record for both paths that a reader can compare line by line, as CULLING's paired rows are.

items.statement: In the valley, on the moving route and under snap turns, every cooked placement's mesh-stage bytes with the cull on equal its bytes with the cull off, at every frame.

Each Sun shadow pass that draws a cooked mesh stores, through the stages with the light's frustum test on, the depth it stores with the test off, to the byte. A pass that a mesh only partly reaches launches fewer mesh workgroups than the mesh has meshlets.
items.ask: Does a diagnostic count show meshlets rejected in a shadow pass on the valley, so the equality is not vacuous?

items.statement: On the mesh-stage path the valley shows its terrain and every cooked mesh whole, with no hole, flicker or popping meshlet, at the route's stops and in motion, at noon and at a low Sun.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills at the route's stops at noon and at a low Sun and a `realtime` sequence of the route on the mesh-stage path, with the same stops on the indirect path beside them, whole and as native-size crops of ridge lines and of mesh edges near the screen's border.

items.statement: An edited cooked mesh switches on the mesh-stage path in the publication's frame, with its placements. No frame draws new meshlet tables against old vertices or old tables against new vertices, and a refused publication changes nothing.
items.ask: Is the switch frame the one the content publication names, from the same run that shows the image change?

items.statement: After a device replacement the path resolves again and draws the bytes it drew before, and a frame that is recorded and discarded leaves the next frame right.

For both paths on the valley's route at 1280×720 and 1920×1080, with the machine's load, the record holds: the CPU time to record the cooked draws, the GPU time of the cull pass, the forward pass and each shadow pass by name, the whole frame, the draws recorded, the meshlets submitted and rejected, and resident bytes. Each tripwire of the design's cost account that the record trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.
items.ask: Are the rows paired and interleaved on this milestone's build, and is the CPU time to record the draws kept apart from GPU time?

items.statement: No exact baseline moves: with no request, and on the direct and indirect paths, every registered image on the Mac's two recipes and in Chrome is the one on main.

milestones.name: The record says whether the object and mesh stages measured faster on this Mac, and the Apple recipe selects them by default only if they did
milestones.quality_bar: A promotion record a reader can trust, as APPLE-TILE's integrated record is: paired, taken in one quiet sitting, each conclusion no stronger than its rows, and nothing claimed for a target that was not run.

items.statement: In one sitting with other builders paused, on the valley's route at 1280×720 and 1920×1080 on the Apple tile recipe with capture off, the paired record holds M2.6's rows for the indirect path and for the mesh stages. Each is run twice, interleaved, and the record gives the spread between its two runs, the load and the thermal state. No figure in the record decides this item.
items.ask: Was the record taken in one sitting with other builders paused, on the final build, with each path run twice and interleaved?

items.statement: The registry's promoted list is what the design's rule gives from that record, `Auto` resolves by it, and the Mac window on the Apple tile recipe asks for `mesh-stages` itself exactly when the path is promoted, while a capture or a test asks only for what it names. The record states its conclusion: promoted, no measurable effect or slower.
items.ask: Do the retained rows support the promoted list the code holds, by the design's rule and no other?

items.statement: On the final build the valley passes M2.3's list on the mesh-stage path.
items.inspect: One capture pass on the final build: `fixed` stills at the route's stops at noon and at a low Sun and a `realtime` sequence of the route on the mesh-stage path, judged by M2.3's list.

items.statement: The record says, from its rows, what share of the valley's cooked triangles the cone and frustum tests removed in each pass and what that saved, and what the same tests would be expected to remove from the exit scene's entities, so that the next plan can decide whether entities are drawn this way.
items.ask: Is the expectation for entities derived from measured shares on meshes like the exit scene's props, with its assumptions stated, and not asserted?

items.statement: A creator can select the path for a scene from the public documentation: the launch request, the scene's request, what it resolves to on a device without the stages, and what was measured.
items.ask: Could an agent that has read only the public documentation launch a scene on the mesh stages on this Mac and read back that it did?

items.statement: The maturity ledger has a row for the mesh-stage path, with implementation, correctness, visuals and device kept apart, and claims nothing for a recipe or a target that was not run.
items.ask: Does the row match what M1 to M3 ran, with the physical iPhone recorded as owed?

items.statement: Every exact baseline holds after promotion, because the verifier's runs name no hardware feature.
